interactions.label: Magnitude of load |F|
interactions.teaches: The same force magnitude produces equal-size but opposite-sign length changes: tension places the deformed end above the original top, while compression places it inside the original rod below the top

demo_steps.title: Original length reference
demo_steps.narration: With |F| = 0, each dashed deformed end coincides with the solid top face. The L0 brackets span the identical original lengths in both panels.

demo_steps.title: Equal and opposite length changes
demo_steps.narration: Increasing |F| separates the dashed end positions from the original top. In panel (a) the dashed end moves upward for tensile strain, while in panel (b) it moves downward inside the rod for compressive strain.

demo_steps.title: Signed strain comparison
demo_steps.narration: At a larger load, the two Delta L brackets have the same magnitude but opposite direction relative to L0. This is the visual basis for tensile strain +Delta L/L0 and compressive strain -Delta L/L0.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a static two-panel comparison by default; do not toggle between panels. Coordinate convention for the axonometric scene: +X is screen-right, +Y is screen-up along the rod axis, and +Z is the receding diagonal used only to give the circular faces depth. Each solid cylinder has identical world dimensions X × Y × Z = 0.9 × 3.0 × 0.9, with radius R = 0.45 in the XZ cross-section and original length L0 = 3.0 along Y. Left cylinder centerline at x = -1.55, right cylinder centerline at x = +1.55; both have bottom level y = 0 and solid top level y = L0 = 3.0. The loadMagnitude slider controls only the displayed deformation offset and arrow length, not the solid cylinder dimensions: use d = DeltaL_visible = 0.65 * loadMagnitude world units. Panel (a), tension: the solid cylinder remains from y=0 to y=3.0; the dashed stretched top ellipse is at y=3.0+d; dashed vertical side guide lines run from the solid top rim to the dashed top ellipse at the left and right silhouette edges. The left panel Delta L bracket must span exactly y=3.0 to y=3.0+d, placed left of the rod at x approximately centerX-0.85; the left panel L0 bracket must span exactly y=0 to y=3.0, directly below it on the same side. Panel (b), compression: the solid cylinder remains from y=0 to y=3.0; the dashed shortened ellipse is inside the cylinder at y=3.0-d; no dashed outline should appear above the compression cylinder. The right panel Delta L bracket must span exactly from y=3.0 down to y=3.0-d, placed right of the rod at x approximately centerX+0.85; the right panel L0 bracket must span y=0 to y=3.0, placed left of the rod at x approximately centerX-0.85. Force arrows are thick red #c93336. Panel (a) top arrow points straight upward along +Y above the dashed/solid top region; panel (a) bottom arrow points straight downward along -Y below the bottom face. Panel (b) top arrow points straight downward toward the top face; panel (b) bottom arrow points straight upward toward the bottom face. Label every force arrow with a vector F symbol. Preferred rendering is italic 'F' plus a small red arrow accent drawn above it, or MathJax/SVG '\vec{F}'; avoid unsupported Unicode combining glyphs that can render as a square. Cylinder fill pale blue-lavender #d6ddf2 with subtle darker side shading #b9c6e3, rim/dashed stroke blue-gray #7f93b3, dimension brackets and labels black #111111. Area label A in panel (b) sits above/right of the top face with a curly leader pointing to the top ellipse. Panel labels '(a)' and '(b)' are centered below the respective cylinders. Mathematical relation for correctness: tensile/compressive strain is epsilon = Delta L / L0, with Delta L positive in tension and negative in compression; cross-sectional area A is held constant in this low-stress linear illustration.
plan.notes: Use an orthographic axonometric camera with a slight top view so the cylinder faces appear as ellipses, not circles, and keep both rods the same apparent width. The solid cylinder height should never change with the slider; only the dashed deformed end positions, Delta L brackets, and optional arrow length change. Dimension bracket endpoints must be anchored to the exact same y-levels as the cylinder bottom, solid top, and dashed deformed-end ellipse. Use dashed LineSegments or curve strokes with a consistent dash pattern for the stretched top outline and compressed internal ellipse. Render labels with an SDF font, SVG text, or HTML overlay so ΔL, L₀, A, panel labels, and vector F remain legible in the PDF reader.

authoredPrompt: This figure places two panels side by side, labeled (a) and (b) beneath them, each a shaded three-dimensional cylinder standing on end and representing the same rod under opposite loading. In panel (a) a thick red arrow labeled F points straight up from above the top face and a matching red arrow labeled F points straight down from below the bottom face; a dashed outline extends above the solid cylinder to mark the stretched portion, bracketed at the left as 'Delta L', with a longer bracket below it spanning the original length 'L0'. In panel (b) the two red arrows are reversed, pressing inward from above and below, a curly leader labels the top circular face 'A', and a bracket labeled 'Delta L' at the right runs from the top face down to a dashed ellipse drawn inside the cylinder where the end formerly sat, with 'L0' bracketed at the left. Both cylinders are drawn at identical width, so the whole comparison rests on whether the dashed reference outline lies outside or inside the solid body. The pairing defines the signed length change from the undeformed length L0 that enters tensile and compressive strain, with the cross-section held constant in the low-stress linear range.
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between tension and compression: the learner switches the loading mode, the red force arrows reverse and the dashed reference moves outside or inside the cylinder, making the sign of Delta L relative to L0 clear.
- Slider for applied force magnitude: the learner drags from compression through zero to tension, the cylinder shortens or lengthens while its cross-section stays fixed, showing the linear low-stress relationship between axial force and length change.
authoredContext:
Tension or compression occurs when two antiparallel forces of equal magnitude act on an object along only one of its dimensions, in such a way that the object does not move. One way to envision such a situation is illustrated in the figure. A rod segment is either stretched or squeezed by a pair of forces acting along its length and perpendicular to its cross-section. The net effect of such forces is that the rod changes its length from the original length L0 that it had before the forces appeared, to a new length L that it has under the action of the forces. This change in length ΔL=L−L0 may be either elongation (when L is larger than the original length L0) or contraction (when L is smaller than the original length L0). Tensile stress and strain occur when the forces are stretching an object, causing its elongation, and the length change ΔL is positive. Compressive stress and strain occur when the forces are contracting an object, causing its shortening, and the length change ΔL is negative.

Compressive stress and strain are defined by the same formulas, the equation and the equation, respectively. The only difference from the tensile situation is that for compressive stress and strain, we take absolute values of the right-hand sides in the equation and the equation.

When an object is in either tension or compression, the net force on it is zero, but the object deforms by changing its original length L0. (a) Tension: The rod is elongated by ΔL. (b) Compression: The rod is contracted by ΔL. In both cases, the deforming force acts along the length of the rod and perpendicular to its cross-section. In the linear range of low stress, the cross-sectional area of the rod does not change.

Figure A is a schematic drawing of a cylinder with a length L0 that is under the tensile strain. Two forces at the different sides of cylinder increase its length by Delta L. Figure B is a schematic drawing of a cylinder with a length L0 that is under the compressive strain. Two forces at the different sides of cylinder reduce its length by Delta L.

Young’s modulus Y is the elastic modulus when deformation is caused by either tensile or compressive stress, and is defined by the equation. Dividing this equation by tensile strain, we obtain the expression for Young’s modulus:

interactions.label: Loading mode
interactions.teaches: Tension and compression differ by the sign of the length change: the original reference end lies outside the stretched rod but inside the shortened rod

interactions.label: Applied force F
interactions.teaches: In the low-stress elastic range, axial length change is proportional to applied force while the cross-sectional area is held fixed

demo_steps.title: Tension: positive Delta L
demo_steps.narration: The red arrows pull outward from the rod ends. The solid cylinder is longer than L0, so the dashed reference top sits below the new top extension and Delta L is positive.

demo_steps.title: Zero load: undeformed length
demo_steps.narration: At F = 0 the dashed reference ellipse coincides with the top face. The measured length change collapses to zero while the radius remains unchanged.

demo_steps.title: Compression: negative Delta L
demo_steps.narration: The red arrows press inward toward the rod. The rod shortens, so the dashed reference top lies above the new top face and Delta L is negative relative to L0.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a single switchable panel rather than showing both textbook panels side by side. World scale: undeformed cylinder radius R = 0.55 units, original length L0 = 3.2 units along +Y, centered at x = 0 with bottom at y = 0 and undeformed top at y = 3.2. Cross-section stays constant at radius 0.55 for all force values. Let signed force f be the appliedForce slider value in [-1, 1]; use DeltaL = 0.55 * f world units for a visibly exaggerated linear elastic deformation. Deformed length is L = L0 + DeltaL. Tension is f > 0: top force arrow points upward above the top face, bottom force arrow points downward below the bottom face, dashed reference ellipse is at y = L0 while the solid top is at y = L0 + DeltaL, and a dashed short cylindrical outline occupies the stretched extension between L0 and L. Compression is f < 0: top force arrow points downward toward the top face, bottom force arrow points upward toward the bottom face, dashed reference ellipse remains at y = L0 inside/above the shortened solid cylinder top at y = L0 + DeltaL, and the Delta L bracket spans downward from the reference level to the compressed top. At f = 0, dashed and solid top ellipses coincide. Left L0 bracket runs from y = 0 to y = L0, placed about 0.95 units left of cylinder center. Delta L bracket is placed left of the cylinder in tension, near the top extension, and right of the cylinder in compression, matching the source figure. Colors: cylinder fill pale blue-lavender #d6ddf2 with subtle vertical gradient, rim stroke blue-gray #7f93b3, dashed reference stroke #7f93b3, force arrows red #c93336, dimension lines black #111111, labels black. Area label A is shown near the upper right of the top face with a curved black leader in compression mode, as in panel (b). Use labels F with vector arrow notation if text rendering supports it, Delta L as ΔL, and original length as L₀. Formula for correctness: DeltaL = F L0 / (Y A), with the displayed slider using normalized F and constant A.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera looking almost front-on but slightly above so the cylinder top appears as an ellipse, not a circle; avoid perspective convergence. Cylinder can be a Three.js CylinderGeometry with open-ended side plus separate ellipse disks/rims, or a custom shaded mesh to keep the textbook-style flat illustration. Update cylinder height, top disk position, dashed reference ellipse, brackets, labels, and arrow directions reactively. The loadingMode toggle should set the sign of appliedForce while preserving its magnitude; the signed slider can also cross zero directly and should update the displayed mode when its sign changes.
